subject: Re: OliveTech production safety-degrade & version-lock request
messages:
From: Jenna Park <jenna.park@olivetech.com>
To: rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: sre@olivetech.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production canary safety - automatic fallback & pinning

Hi Rachel,

Quick note from our side — after last week's partial canary we saw a ~12% spike in 95p latency for requests routed to the new small-quant model variant. Our product team is nervous about rolling the A/B to 20% without an automatic safety net.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood enable an automatic-degrade policy that reverts traffic to the previous pinned model if 95p latency breaches our agreed SLO for 3 consecutive minutes?
- Can we pin the previous stable model and have a short cool-down before any subsequent automated rollout so we don't flip-flop?

We'd like to formalize this as a short-term SLA carve-out while we finish the performance tuning. Can we schedule a call to confirm exact thresholds (95p latency vs error rate) and the implementation approach?

Thanks — Jenna
Jenna Park
Senior PM, OliveTech

Attachments: slo-matrix-olive-v1.xlsx (requested thresholds template)

From: rachel_kim@redwood.ai
To: Jenna Park <jenna.park@olivetech.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production canary safety - automatic fallback & pinning

Jenna — thanks for the clear ask. Happy to get this locked down quickly. Proposed next steps:

1) Temporary SLA mitigation: we can authorize an automated fallback that triggers if 95p latency > 400ms for 3 consecutive minutes OR error rate > 1.5% for 2 consecutive minutes. Fallback will route 100% of traffic back to the pinned stable model version.

2) Pin / cool-down: we support a version-lock window (default 15 minutes) after an automated fallback. During that window, the model stays pinned and no auto-rollouts will execute unless manually overridden by your SRE.

3) Conditional approvals: we'll provision the policy in your Dedicated pool as a short-lived exception while you complete perf tuning. After 30 days we revisit to make it part of standard rollout runbooks or remove it.

I cc'd Marcus (runtime lead) and Lauren (your account lead) — Marcus, are there any infra caveats (KV cache, prefix warmup) we should call out for OliveTech's traffic profile? Lauren — need your sign-off for the SLA carve-out and to record the exception in the account record.

I attached a short playbook draft naming the thresholds and the rollback behavior. If that looks good to you both, I'll schedule a 30-minute sync with OliveTech tomorrow.

— Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: safety-net-playbook.pdf

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: rachel_kim@redwood.ai, Jenna Park <jenna.park@olivetech.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production canary safety - automatic fallback & pinning

Thanks Rachel — technical ack from our side. A few implementation notes so OliveTech has full visibility:

- Automatic fallback is doable. We'll implement a short-circuit that swaps routing to the pinned model variant and clears any active KV cache for requests so the fallback has a clean baseline.
- Caveat: there will be a brief tokenization/latency penalty during the first 30s after fallback as KV cache warms; recommend making the fallback window "minimum pin 5 minutes" to avoid oscillation.
- For your threshold values, I suggest starting with 95p > 420ms (since your workload has long tail tokens) and error > 1.2% (our error taxonomy filters transient HTTP3 retries). We can tune these after two canary runs.
- I'll add circuit-breaker metrics to the rollout trace and a dedicated alert to OliveTech's PagerDuty.

If OliveTech agrees, we can push this as a scoped Dedicated policy today and enable the Drive playbook link.

— Marcus Lin
Lead, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: rachel_kim@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, Jenna Park <jenna.park@olivetech.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production canary safety - automatic fallback & pinning

All — I approve the temporary SLA exception under the following commercial terms:

- Exception window: 30 days (2027-06-12 through 2027-07-12)
- No changes to list price; Redwood will provide one-time onboarding support (2 engineer-days) at no charge to instrument fallback observability and alerts.
- OliveTech must confirm escape hatch procedures and a single SRE owner for manual overrides (documented in the Drive playbook).

Next steps: Rachel, please capture this in the HubSpot record and create the exception entry referencing deal OL V-2027-Q2-9 (HubSpot: 82077). Marcus, please push the policy to OliveTech's Dedicated pool and set the initial thresholds to 95p > 420ms / error > 1.2% with a 5-minute minimum pin. Jenna, once your SRE confirms the PagerDuty rotation, we'll flip the switch.

Thanks — Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Sales Director, Redwood Inference
